arxiv-1911-11544.title: Image2StyleGAN++: How to Edit the Embedded Images?
arxiv-1911-11544.creator: Rameen Abdal, Yipeng Qin, Peter Wonka
arxiv-1911-11544.description: Abstract We propose Image2StyleGAN++, a flexible image editing framework with many applications. Our framework extends the recent Image2StyleGAN [ 1 ] in three ways. First, we introduce noise optimization as a complement to the W + W^{+} latent space embedding. Our noise optimization can restore high frequency features in images and thus significantly improves the quality of reconstructed images, e.

arxiv-2008-11025.title: Poisson orders on large quantum groups Thanks: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. DMS-1440140 while N. A. was in residence at the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute in Berkeley, California, in the Spring 2020 semester. The work of N. A
arxiv-2008-11025.creator: Nicolás Andruskiewitsch, Iván Angiono, Milen Yakimov
arxiv-2008-11025.description: Abstract . We develop a Poisson geometric framework for studying the representation theory of all contragredient quantum super groups at roots of unity. This is done in a uniform fashion by treating the larger class of quantum doubles of bozonizations of all distinguished pre-Nichols algebras [ 9 ] belonging to a one-parameter family; we call these algebras large quantum groups.

arxiv-2010-08051.title: Program Equivalence for Assisted Grading of Functional Programs (Extended Version) CCS: Theory of computation Automated reasoning
arxiv-2010-08051.creator: Joshua Clune, Vijay Ramamurthy, Ruben Martins, Umut A. Acar
arxiv-2010-08051.description: Abstract . In courses that involve programming assignments, giving meaningful feedback to students is an important challenge. Human beings can give useful feedback by manually grading the programs but this is a time-consuming, labor intensive, and usually boring process. Automatic graders can be fast and scale well but they usually provide poor feedback.

arxiv-2110-07882.title: PolyNet: Polynomial Neural Network for 3D Shape Recognition with PolyShape Representation
arxiv-2110-07882.creator: Mohsen Yavartanoo 1 Shih-Hsuan Hung 2 Reyhaneh Neshatavar 1 Yue Zhang 2 Kyoung Mu Lee 1 1 SNU ECE & ASRI 2 Oregon State University {myavartanoo,reyhanehneshat,kyoungmu}@snu.ac.kr {hungsh,zhangyue}@oregonstate.edu
arxiv-2110-07882.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mohsen Yavartanoo 1 Shih-Hsuan Hung 2 Reyhaneh Neshatavar 1 Yue Zhang 2 Kyoung Mu Lee 1 1 SNU ECE & ASRI 2 Oregon State University {myavartanoo,reyhanehneshat,kyoungmu}@snu.ac.kr {hungsh,zhangyue}@oregonstate.edu. 3D shape representation and its processing have substantial effects on 3D shape recognition. The polygon mesh as a 3D shape representation has many advantages in computer graphics and geometry processing.

arxiv-2110-09916.title: Identification of high order closure terms from fully kinetic simulations using machine learning Preprint: DOI: 10.1063/5.0066397
arxiv-2110-09916.creator: B. Laperre, J. Amaya, S. Jamal, G. Lapenta
arxiv-2110-09916.description: Abstract Simulations of large-scale plasma systems are typically based on a fluid approximation approach. These models construct a moment-based system of equations that approximate the particle-based physics as a fluid, but as a result lack the small-scale physical processes available to fully kinetic models.

arxiv-2112-07398.title: A hybrid integrated dual-microcomb source
arxiv-2112-07398.creator: Nikita Yu. Dmitriev, Sergey N. Koptyaev, Andrey S. Voloshin, Nikita M. Kondratiev, Valery E. Lobanov, Kirill N. Min’kov, Maxim V. Ryabko, Stanislav V. Polonsky, Igor A. Bilenko
arxiv-2112-07398.description: Abstract Abstract Dual-comb interferometry is based on self-heterodyning two optical frequency combs, with corresponding mapping of the optical spectrum into the radio-frequency domain. The dual-comb enables diverse applications, including metrology, fast high-precision spectroscopy with high signal-to-noise ratio, distance ranging, and coherent optical communications.

arxiv-2302-10441.title: Speech Privacy Leakage from Shared Gradients in Distributed Learning
arxiv-2302-10441.creator: Zhuohang Li, Jiaxin Zhang, Jian Liu
arxiv-2302-10441.description: Abstract Distributed machine learning paradigms, such as federated learning, have been recently adopted in many privacy-critical applications for speech analysis. However, such frameworks are vulnerable to privacy leakage attacks from shared gradients. Despite extensive efforts in the image domain, the exploration of speech privacy leakage from gradients is quite limited.

arxiv-2310-12657.title: 4-Cycle Free Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes with an Explicit Construction
arxiv-2310-12657.creator: Zeinab Roostaie, Mohammad Gholami, Farzad Parvaresh
arxiv-2310-12657.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zeinab Roostaie, Mohammad Gholami, Farzad Parvaresh. Spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes are a class of capacity approaching LDPC codes with low message recovery latency when a sliding window decoding is used. In this paper, we first present a new method for the construction of a class of SC-LDPC codes by the incidence matrices of a given non-negative integer matrix E E , and then the relationship of 4-cycles between matrix E E and the corresponding SC-LDPC code are investigated.

arxiv-2502-10159.title: The hadronic contribution to the running of α \alpha and the electroweak mixing angle
arxiv-2502-10159.creator: Hartmut Wittig
arxiv-2502-10159.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hartmut Wittig. We report on our update to [ 1 ] on the hadronic running of electroweak couplings from O ⁡ ( a ) O(a) -improved Wilson fermions with N f = 2 + 1 N_{f}=2+1 flavours. The inclusion of additional ensembles at very fine lattice spacings together with a number of techniques to split the different contributions for a better control of cutoff effects allows us to substantially improve the precision.

arxiv-2507-13069.title: A kinematic and structural study of young open clusters in the Milky Way Galaxy using Gaia DR3 catalogue
arxiv-2507-13069.creator: Harsha K H 1,2,*, Annapurni Subramaniam 2, S. R. Dhanush 2,3, and Harharan D S 4
arxiv-2507-13069.description: Abstract We aim to identify the cluster members, estimate cluster properties, study the dynamical state of the clusters as a function of mass, trace the existence of dynamical effects in massive stars, and check for spatial patterns of members in young clusters.

arxiv-2508-15125.title: Modeling pandemics
arxiv-2508-15125.creator: John F. Dawson, Fred Cooper, Efstathios G. Charalampidis
arxiv-2508-15125.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by John F. Dawson, Fred Cooper, Efstathios G. Charalampidis. We review several models for pandemics that plagued the USA and the world in the past decade. Methods of data fitting are reviewed and several types of microscopic and rate equation models are discussed and numerically solved. This paper was written in March of 2021 and newer data is now available; however some of the models and techniques we used to numerically study these models are still of interest. Several appendices discuss in detail these models.

arxiv-2601-04716.title: Fame Fades, Nature Remains: Disentangling the Character Identity of Role-Playing Agents
arxiv-2601-04716.creator: Yonghyun Jun, Junhyuk Choi, Jihyeong Park, Hwanhee Lee
arxiv-2601-04716.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yonghyun Jun, Junhyuk Choi, Jihyeong Park, Hwanhee Lee. Despite the rapid proliferation of Role-Playing Agents (RPAs) based on Large Language Models (LLMs), the structural dimensions defining a character’s identity remain weakly formalized, often treating characters as arbitrary text inputs.

arxiv-2602-10527.title: AI-PACE: A Framework for Integrating AI into Medical Education
arxiv-2602-10527.creator: Scott P. McGrath, Katherine K. Kim, Karnjit Johl, Haibo Wang, Nick Anderson
arxiv-2602-10527.description: Abstract The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare is accelerating, yet medical education has not kept pace with these technological advancements. This paper synthesizes current knowledge on AI in medical education through a comprehensive analysis of the literature, identifying key competencies, curricular approaches, and implementation strategies.

pmc-10531811.title: Optimization of Production Methods for Black Soldier Fly Larvae (Hermetia illucens L.) in Burkina Faso
pmc-10531811.creator: Florence Sankara, Fernand Sankara, Salimata Pousga, Kalifa Coulibaly, Jacques Philippe Nacoulma, Zakaria Ilboudo, Issoufou Ouédraogo, Irénée Somda, Marc Kenis
pmc-10531811.description: Simple SummaryThe black soldier fly is a tropical and subtropical fly that is increasingly used in animal feed worldwide. Its larvae develop in organic plant or animal matter and agro-industrial by-products. In Africa, they represent a source of protein that can help improve local poultry feed rations.

pmc-10595574.title: Shifting towards a Well-being Economy in Wales for a fairer, sustainable and healthier society
pmc-10595574.creator: A Stielke, K Ashton, M Dyakova
pmc-10595574.description: Wales, and other nations globally, face long-standing challenges such as climate change and on-going impacts of the pandemic. This has increased persisting health inequities, widening the health gap and putting health and social systems and other public services under even more pressure.

pmc-11472302.title: Reevaluation of ADHD diagnoses in referral patients: A medical chart review in an advanced psychiatric hospital in Japan
pmc-11472302.creator: Kosuke Suzuki, Tomihisa Niitsu, Maria Kato, Masaomi Iyo
pmc-11472302.description: Our study examined the diagnostic accuracy of ADHD among referral patients, revealing that 66% had confirmed ADHD while 24% had their diagnosis changed, primarily to bipolar disorder. These findings emphasize the need for comprehensive evaluation and multidisciplinary collaboration to ensure accurate diagnosis and effective treatment. Attention‐deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often coexists with various comorbidities, particularly bipolar disorder (BD).

pmc-12650224.title: Association Between Renal Cell Cancer and Chronic Kidney Disease: An Update on a Never-Healing Wound
pmc-12650224.creator: Ilias Giannakodimos, Aris Kaltsas, Andreas Koumenis, Evangelia Mitakidi, Konstantinos Adamos, Dimitrios Deligiannis, Marios Stavropoulos, Zisis Kratiras, Michael Chrisofos, Andrea Angioi
pmc-12650224.description: The relationship between chronic kidney disease (CKD) and renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is both bidirectional and multifactorial. Several risk factors, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, obesity, and smoking, have been associated with an increased risk for the development of CKD and RCC. CKD may predispose individuals to RCC through various mechanisms, including renal cystic diseases or induced oxidative stress effects.

pmc-12709827.title: A population-based survey of beliefs about neck pain and its associated disorders: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12709827.creator: Mirella Forte, Federica Nasti, Stefano Schiavone, Matteo Cioeta, Graziana Lullo, Fabio Cataldi, Giuseppe Giovannico, Filippo Maselli, Ian Young, James Dunning, Daniel Feller, Firas Mourad
pmc-12709827.description: BackgroundNeck pain and whiplash are prevalent disorders with high socio-economic burden. Beliefs and expectations influence their prognosis, causing chronicisation. We aimed to investigate the perspective of the Italian population.MethodsWe conducted an online survey among Italian adults recruited through social media. The main outcomes were the Whiplash Beliefs Questionnaire (WBQ) total score and its subscales, recovery expectations, and anxiety/stress items.

pmc-12959464.title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices Towards Hepatitis B Infection Among Nursing Students: A Cross‐Sectional Study in Jordan
pmc-12959464.creator: Nader Alaridah, Raba'a F Jarrar, Rayan M Joudeh, Mallak Aljarawen, Hasan Nassr, Rahaf A Jereisat, Arwa battah, Mohammad Jum'ah, Noor Rajeh Abu Hantash, Mohammad Nour Amr, Haneen Al‐Abdallat, Layan Ismail, Anas Y El‐Massad, Heba Mahmmoud, Anas H A Abu‐Humaidan
pmc-12959464.description: Background and AimsHepatitis B is a serious, communicable liver disease resulting from hepatitis B virus infection. Healthcare workers (HCWs), including nursing students, are at elevated risk of exposure. We assessed Jordanian nursing students' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward HBV and explored predictors of better KAP.

pmc-13062338.title: Uncoupling of the Helical Blade in a Proximal Femoral Nail – A Novel Mechanical Failure
pmc-13062338.creator: Anurag Bhakhar, Anil Kumar, Bhaskar Sarkar, Nirvin Paul, Arvind Kumar Yadav, Md. Quamar Azam
pmc-13062338.description: Introduction:Intertrochanteric fractures are increasingly common in the elderly, and intramedullary fixation with a proximal femoral nail antirotation (PFNA) is widely preferred due to its biomechanical advantages. The helical blade improves cancellous bone purchase, yet complications such as cut-out, cut-in, and excessive sliding remain concerns. Mechanical uncoupling of the helical blade from the nail is extremely rare.

pmc-13475411.title: The Effects of Ambient Air Pollutants on Changes in Cardiac Structure and Function
pmc-13475411.creator: Claire L. Leiser, Daniela Sotres-Alvarez, Haeyoon Chang, Elizabeth W. Spalt, Barry E. Hurwitz, Martha L. Daviglus, Greg Talavera, Robert Kaplan, Bonnie E. Shook-Sa, Carlos J. Rodriguez, Joel D. Kaufman
pmc-13475411.description: BackgroundThe effects of air pollutants on cardiac structure and function preceding the clinical diagnosis of heart failure are not well understood.ObjectivesThe objective of the study was to determine if ambient pollutant concentrations are associated with longitudinal changes in cardiac structure and function.
